# Atomicals and ARC-20

> The working reference for Atomicals digital objects, ARC-20 tokens, and the Universe services that expose them.
> Documentation version: 2026.08
> Home: https://bitcoinuniverseio.github.io/atomicals-and-arc-20/
> Full content: /atomicals-and-arc-20/llms-full.txt
> Page manifest: /atomicals-and-arc-20/manifest.json
> Raw Markdown for any page: /atomicals-and-arc-20/raw/<page-id>.md
> Verified: 2026-08-31

## How to read this documentation

Three layers are never mixed, and every page states which one it describes:

- Protocol behavior: what a pinned Atomicals validator revision does.
- Universe implementation: what a Bitcoin Universe service actually exposes today.
- Proposed or experimental: what exists but is not live.

A protocol capability is not automatically a product feature. A product feature is not
automatically protocol behavior. A proposal is not an implementation.

## Normative sources, in authority order

1. Executed source code, conformance tests, generated inventories, schemas, and runtime
   contracts at an exact revision.
2. Final or Living Atomicals Improvement Proposals.
3. The Atomicals reference implementation at an exact commit or release.
4. Official Atomicals protocol and CLI documentation.
5. Universe implementation documentation at an exact revision.
6. Third-party integrations, always non-normative.

Explanatory prose, including this documentation, is never independent consensus.

## The ARC-20 model in seven statements

1. One ARC-20 unit is one satoshi in an output a validator recognises as coloured.
2. Supply is therefore measured in satoshis and bounded by real bitcoin.
3. Issuance is direct, fixed decentralised, or activation gated perpetual.
4. A ticker is a globally allocated name resolved to exactly one Atomical. It is not identity.
5. A transfer is an allocation over the transaction's inputs and outputs, in order.
6. Value that cannot be placed in an eligible output is destroyed. The transaction still confirms.
7. Coloured output totals can never exceed coloured input totals.

## Executed allocation vectors

Engine: conformance/allocation.mjs, implemented from atomicals-electrumx-1.5.2.0 at 8df23747835c20230fc8b8097d469e7a1d97c3e0.
Vectors: /atomicals-and-arc-20/conformance/vectors/arc20-allocation.json

- clean-split: Both outputs are exactly covered, so nothing is left to place and nothing burns.
- oversized-next-output: Output zero takes 700. The next output is 546 satoshis, larger than the 500 units left, so the remainder is destroyed.
- exact-single-output: One output exactly equal to the coloured value takes everything.
- first-output-too-large: Nothing can be placed at all, so the entire coloured value is destroyed.
- too-few-outputs: Every output is covered but value is still left over, so the leftover burns.
- unspendable-output-skipped: A provably unspendable output is passed over and consumes no coloured value.
- combine-two-lots: Two coloured inputs of the same token are summed before allocation and land in one output.
- two-tokens-sequential-slots: The first token fills the outputs it needs, then the next token starts after the last slot the first one used.
- two-tokens-non-clean-fallback: When the sequential assignment cannot be made cleanly, the reference builder restarts every token from output zero. Both tokens then contend for the same outputs and value burns.
- dust-remainder-burns: Sending 1000 units from a 1200 unit lot with a 200 satoshi change output fails, because 200 is placed only if it fits after the 1000 is taken. Here it does fit, so nothing burns. Compare with the next case.
- change-output-too-large: The same intent with a 546 satoshi change output destroys the 200 unit remainder, because 546 does not fit in 200.
- custom-coloring-partial-fill: With custom coloring active the builder attaches an output even when the value does not cover it fully, and the last output receives only what is left.
- suite-exact-single-output: The token exactly fills the only output, so nothing is left over and the assignment is clean.
- suite-partially-colored-carry-forward: Since height 848484 an output can carry fewer token units than satoshis. The 500 units land on an 11000 satoshi output and nothing burns. Reported as not cleanly assigned because the output is only partly coloured.
- suite-consolidation-burn: The classic consolidation accident: everything beyond the first output is destroyed.
- suite-output-over-balance: Under exact-cover rules an output has to be fully covered. Being one satoshi short colours nothing at all. The same shape under current rules colours the output partially and burns nothing, which is why the rule changed.
- suite-one-unit-over: The single leftover unit is the miner fee, and it is burned token supply.
- suite-merged-inputs-single-output: The pool is 1455, the output takes 1454, and the remaining unit is burned.
- suite-no-atomicals: Spending no token-bearing input produces an empty blueprint. An implementation must not fabricate assignments for an uncoloured transaction.
- fee-taken-from-colored-value: The outputs total 200 satoshis less than the coloured input, and those 200 units are destroyed rather than returned. Pay the fee from a plain bitcoin input instead.
- only-unspendable-outputs: Unspendable outputs are skipped by regular assignment, so a transaction whose only output is an OP_RETURN leaves the balance nowhere to land.
- split-skip-amount: The y payload names satoshis to pass over before a token starts colouring, which is how two tokens sharing one input get separated. Here output 0 satisfies the skip, the token colours output 1, and the value beyond it burns.
- custom-color-over-request-clamped: The payload asks for more than either token holds. Each request is clamped to the output value and then to the remaining balance, so no inflation is possible.
- custom-color-unassigned-value-burns: The payload directs 400 units at output 0 and says nothing about the rest, so the remaining 600 units are destroyed. Custom colouring places value explicitly; it does not carry a remainder forward.

## What is never claimed here

- No price, market, ranking, investment, legal, or tax statement.
- Metadata is never authenticity. A ticker is never creator identity. A listing is never ownership.
- An indexer result is version scoped, never consensus.
- A configured service is never automatically ready.
- A proposal is never an implemented feature.

### start

- [Choose your path](https://bitcoinuniverseio.github.io/atomicals-and-arc-20/start/choose-your-path/) [editorial]: Four short routes through this documentation, one for each thing people actually come here to do.
- [Glossary](https://bitcoinuniverseio.github.io/atomicals-and-arc-20/start/glossary/) [protocol-behavior]: Every Atomicals and ARC-20 term used on this site, defined once and used consistently everywhere.
- [Networks and versions](https://bitcoinuniverseio.github.io/atomicals-and-arc-20/start/networks-and-versions/) [protocol-behavior]: Which network a statement applies to, which validator revision decides it, and which documentation version you are reading.
- [Protocol family map](https://bitcoinuniverseio.github.io/atomicals-and-arc-20/start/protocol-family-map/) [protocol-behavior]: Every Atomicals primitive in one place, what it produces, which operation creates it, and where Universe exposes it today.
- [Safety fundamentals](https://bitcoinuniverseio.github.io/atomicals-and-arc-20/start/safety-fundamentals/) [protocol-behavior]: The eight checks that separate a clean Atomicals transaction from a permanent loss, and the four claims you must never accept at face value.
- [Status and known limitations](https://bitcoinuniverseio.github.io/atomicals-and-arc-20/start/status-and-limitations/) [universe-implementation]: What is live, what is beta, what is proposed, what is not exposed at all, and the limitations we know about and have not hidden.
- [What are Atomicals?](https://bitcoinuniverseio.github.io/atomicals-and-arc-20/start/what-are-atomicals/) [protocol-behavior]: Digital objects that live inside ordinary Bitcoin outputs, identified by the transaction that created them and interpreted by an Atomicals validator.
- [What is ARC-20?](https://bitcoinuniverseio.github.io/atomicals-and-arc-20/start/what-is-arc-20/) [protocol-behavior]: The Atomicals fungible token model, where one unit is one coloured satoshi and transfers are an allocation problem rather than an account update.

### protocol

- [Atomicals Improvement Proposals](https://bitcoinuniverseio.github.io/atomicals-and-arc-20/protocol/aips/) [proposed]: The AIP register, the complete status model, and implementation evidence that is never assumed from a proposal existing.
- [Allocation](https://bitcoinuniverseio.github.io/atomicals-and-arc-20/protocol/arc20/allocation/) [protocol-behavior]: The exact rule a validator uses to place coloured value into outputs, with executed vectors for every case.
- [ARC-20 Bitwork requirements](https://bitcoinuniverseio.github.io/atomicals-and-arc-20/protocol/arc20/bitwork-requirements/) [protocol-behavior]: Which Bitwork fields apply to a deployment, which apply to its claimants, and how to read them correctly.
- [Burns](https://bitcoinuniverseio.github.io/atomicals-and-arc-20/protocol/arc20/burns/) [protocol-behavior]: How ARC-20 value is destroyed, the four shapes that cause it, and the checks that prevent every one of them.
- [Decentralised mint claims](https://bitcoinuniverseio.github.io/atomicals-and-arc-20/protocol/arc20/decentralized-mint/) [protocol-behavior]: What makes a dmt claim valid, why a confirmed claim can still be worthless, and what a minter should check first.
- [Direct FT issuance](https://bitcoinuniverseio.github.io/atomicals-and-arc-20/protocol/arc20/direct-issuance/) [protocol-behavior]: One transaction, one complete supply, entirely in output zero, and why that makes large supplies expensive.
- [Fixed DFT deployment](https://bitcoinuniverseio.github.io/atomicals-and-arc-20/protocol/arc20/fixed-dft/) [protocol-behavior]: The parameters a fixed decentralised deployment sets, what they bound, and what a client must check before treating one as valid.
- [Metadata and decimals](https://bitcoinuniverseio.github.io/atomicals-and-arc-20/protocol/arc20/metadata-and-decimals/) [protocol-behavior]: Optional metadata fields, how to treat them, and the exact rule about decimals that prevents an entire class of accounting bug.
- [ARC-20](https://bitcoinuniverseio.github.io/atomicals-and-arc-20/protocol/arc20/overview/) [protocol-behavior]: The complete ARC-20 model in one page, from issuance through allocation to the safety boundary, with links to the exact rule for each part.
- [Perpetual DFT](https://bitcoinuniverseio.github.io/atomicals-and-arc-20/protocol/arc20/perpetual-dft/) [protocol-behavior]: A separate activation gated mode with progressing Bitwork and an optional global cap, and why it is not fixed DFT with a large number.
- [PSBT requirements](https://bitcoinuniverseio.github.io/atomicals-and-arc-20/protocol/arc20/psbt-requirements/) [protocol-behavior]: What a partially signed transaction must contain for an Atomicals aware wallet to sign it safely, and what a wallet must show you.
- [Split and combine](https://bitcoinuniverseio.github.io/atomicals-and-arc-20/protocol/arc20/split-and-combine/) [protocol-behavior]: Separating coloured lots with the split operation, recombining them, and the activation gated custom coloring path.
- [Substantiation Factor](https://bitcoinuniverseio.github.io/atomicals-and-arc-20/protocol/arc20/substantiation-factor/) [proposed]: What this material is, what status it has, and what evidence would be required before any of it could be presented as behavior.
- [Tickers and candidates](https://bitcoinuniverseio.github.io/atomicals-and-arc-20/protocol/arc20/tickers-and-candidates/) [protocol-behavior]: How an ARC-20 name is requested, resolved, and displayed, and what winning it actually means.
- [Transfers and swaps](https://bitcoinuniverseio.github.io/atomicals-and-arc-20/protocol/arc20/transfers-and-swaps/) [protocol-behavior]: Ordinary transfers, atomic swaps, and the exact output binding that makes a swap safe to sign.
- [The unit model](https://bitcoinuniverseio.github.io/atomicals-and-arc-20/protocol/arc20/unit-model/) [protocol-behavior]: One coloured satoshi is one unit, supply is measured in satoshis, and decimals are presentation only.
- [Wallet safety](https://bitcoinuniverseio.github.io/atomicals-and-arc-20/protocol/arc20/wallet-safety/) [protocol-behavior]: What an Atomicals aware wallet must do, what it must never do, and how to tell whether the wallet you use qualifies.
- [AVM opcodes](https://bitcoinuniverseio.github.io/atomicals-and-arc-20/protocol/avm/opcodes/) [experimental]: The complete opcode inventory generated from the interpreter source, with the upstream test annotation preserved per opcode.
- [AVM](https://bitcoinuniverseio.github.io/atomicals-and-arc-20/protocol/avm/overview/) [experimental]: The Atomicals Virtual Machine, split into the four separate status layers people usually collapse into one.
- [AVM state and execution](https://bitcoinuniverseio.github.io/atomicals-and-arc-20/protocol/avm/state-and-execution/) [experimental]: What a contract call receives, what it returns, and how state is expected to be carried between calls.
- [AVM status and limitations](https://bitcoinuniverseio.github.io/atomicals-and-arc-20/protocol/avm/status-and-limitations/) [experimental]: The exact status of every AVM layer, the threat model, and the evidence that would be required to change any of it.
- [DMINT](https://bitcoinuniverseio.github.io/atomicals-and-arc-20/protocol/containers/dmint/) [protocol-behavior]: Decentralised item minting against a sealed manifest, how verification works, and every failure state a claimant can hit.
- [Item verification](https://bitcoinuniverseio.github.io/atomicals-and-arc-20/protocol/containers/item-verification/) [protocol-behavior]: How to prove an item belongs to a Container, what each check establishes, and what a product must show.
- [Containers](https://bitcoinuniverseio.github.io/atomicals-and-arc-20/protocol/containers/overview/) [protocol-behavior]: A named collection identity that items can prove membership in, and what it takes to make that proof meaningful.
- [Sealing and rules](https://bitcoinuniverseio.github.io/atomicals-and-arc-20/protocol/containers/sealing-and-rules/) [protocol-behavior]: What sealing changes, why rule evaluation must be deterministic, and the order of operations that makes a collection trustworthy.
- [Activation boundaries](https://bitcoinuniverseio.github.io/atomicals-and-arc-20/protocol/core/activation-boundaries/) [protocol-behavior]: Why the same transaction can be valid at one height and invalid at another, and how to reason about rules that turn on.
- [Bitwork](https://bitcoinuniverseio.github.io/atomicals-and-arc-20/protocol/core/bitwork/) [protocol-behavior]: The proof of work prefix requirement that gates Atomicals mints, what it costs, and what it does not promise.
- [Candidates and winners](https://bitcoinuniverseio.github.io/atomicals-and-arc-20/protocol/core/candidates-and-winners/) [protocol-behavior]: Why a name request is not a name, how a candidate becomes a verified winner, and what a product must show while resolution is pending.
- [Commit and reveal](https://bitcoinuniverseio.github.io/atomicals-and-arc-20/protocol/core/commit-and-reveal/) [protocol-behavior]: The two transaction pattern every Atomicals operation uses, and what can go wrong between the two steps.
- [Confirmation and reorgs](https://bitcoinuniverseio.github.io/atomicals-and-arc-20/protocol/core/confirmation-and-reorgs/) [protocol-behavior]: Two separate questions that people constantly merge into one, and what a reorg actually does to an Atomicals result.
- [Atomicals digital objects](https://bitcoinuniverseio.github.io/atomicals-and-arc-20/protocol/core/digital-objects/) [protocol-behavior]: What an Atomical actually is at the data level, what a validator stores about it, and what it never guarantees.
- [Envelope and operations](https://bitcoinuniverseio.github.io/atomicals-and-arc-20/protocol/core/envelope-and-operations/) [protocol-behavior]: The structure a validator reads, the operation codes it recognises, and why a JSON object in a user interface is not a wire format.
- [Identifiers and numbers](https://bitcoinuniverseio.github.io/atomicals-and-arc-20/protocol/core/identifiers/) [protocol-behavior]: Atomical IDs, compact IDs, locations, numbers, and which one to store in your database.
- [Indexer and validator dependency](https://bitcoinuniverseio.github.io/atomicals-and-arc-20/protocol/core/indexer-dependency/) [protocol-behavior]: Why every Atomicals answer is version scoped, and how to handle two sources that disagree.
- [Metadata trust boundaries](https://bitcoinuniverseio.github.io/atomicals-and-arc-20/protocol/core/metadata-trust/) [protocol-behavior]: Everything in a payload is attacker controlled. This page says exactly what that means for a renderer, an indexer, and a user interface.
- [Permanent file storage](https://bitcoinuniverseio.github.io/atomicals-and-arc-20/protocol/core/permanent-storage/) [protocol-behavior]: How Atomicals stores bytes on Bitcoin, what a digest proves, and the limits of treating a chain as a file system.
- [References and recursion](https://bitcoinuniverseio.github.io/atomicals-and-arc-20/protocol/core/references-and-recursion/) [protocol-behavior]: How one Atomical points at another, why recursive rendering needs an archive, and the failure modes of a broken reference.
- [State, history, and updates](https://bitcoinuniverseio.github.io/atomicals-and-arc-20/protocol/core/state-and-history/) [protocol-behavior]: How mutable state works on an Atomical, what history records, and what sealing permanently changes.
- [UTXO ownership and location](https://bitcoinuniverseio.github.io/atomicals-and-arc-20/protocol/core/utxo-ownership/) [protocol-behavior]: Ownership in Atomicals is control of a specific unspent output, not an entry against an address.
- [Collections and Containers](https://bitcoinuniverseio.github.io/atomicals-and-arc-20/protocol/nft/collections-and-containers/) [protocol-behavior]: How an NFT proves membership in a collection, what a Container adds, and what a collection label alone proves.
- [NFT marketplace behavior](https://bitcoinuniverseio.github.io/atomicals-and-arc-20/protocol/nft/marketplace/) [universe-implementation]: What the Marketplace authority checks before an NFT listing, purchase, or settlement is allowed to proceed.
- [Metadata and media](https://bitcoinuniverseio.github.io/atomicals-and-arc-20/protocol/nft/metadata-and-media/) [protocol-behavior]: How an NFT carries files, what a digest guarantees, and the rules a renderer must follow to serve hostile content safely.
- [Minting an NFT](https://bitcoinuniverseio.github.io/atomicals-and-arc-20/protocol/nft/minting/) [protocol-behavior]: What a mint payload contains, what output zero receives, and the decisions that cannot be changed later.
- [Atomicals NFTs](https://bitcoinuniverseio.github.io/atomicals-and-arc-20/protocol/nft/overview/) [protocol-behavior]: Non-fungible Atomicals, what they carry, how they move, and the hazards that come from sharing an output.
- [Splat and mixed outputs](https://bitcoinuniverseio.github.io/atomicals-and-arc-20/protocol/nft/splat-and-mixed-outputs/) [protocol-behavior]: What happens when one output carries several Atomicals, why that is dangerous, and how splat separates them.
- [NFT transfers](https://bitcoinuniverseio.github.io/atomicals-and-arc-20/protocol/nft/transfers/) [protocol-behavior]: Normal transfers, swap transfers, and what a non-fungible move actually commits to.
- [Atomicals protocol](https://bitcoinuniverseio.github.io/atomicals-and-arc-20/protocol/overview/) [protocol-behavior]: One page that puts every Atomicals primitive, operation, and validation boundary in relation to each other.
- [Claims and rules](https://bitcoinuniverseio.github.io/atomicals-and-arc-20/protocol/realms/claims-and-rules/) [protocol-behavior]: How a name claim is evaluated, how payments participate, and why deterministic rules are the whole point.
- [Realm marketplace behavior](https://bitcoinuniverseio.github.io/atomicals-and-arc-20/protocol/realms/marketplace/) [universe-implementation]: What the Marketplace authority checks for Realm and Subrealm listings, and why names have an extra verification step.
- [Realms](https://bitcoinuniverseio.github.io/atomicals-and-arc-20/protocol/realms/overview/) [protocol-behavior]: Top-level Atomicals names, how they are claimed and resolved, and what a name actually establishes.
- [Paynames](https://bitcoinuniverseio.github.io/atomicals-and-arc-20/protocol/realms/paynames/) [protocol-behavior]: Using a Realm as a payment destination, what resolution guarantees, and the checks a payer must run first.
- [Subrealms](https://bitcoinuniverseio.github.io/atomicals-and-arc-20/protocol/realms/subrealms/) [protocol-behavior]: Child names claimed under a parent Realm's rules, how the parent controls them, and what a claimant must satisfy.
- [Unicode, IDNA, and confusable names](https://bitcoinuniverseio.github.io/atomicals-and-arc-20/protocol/realms/unicode-and-idna/) [protocol-behavior]: Why two names that look identical can be different strings, what normalisation does, and the warnings a product must show.

### guides

- [Guides](https://bitcoinuniverseio.github.io/atomicals-and-arc-20/guides/) [editorial]: Task-oriented procedures for holding, inspecting, issuing, moving, and trading Atomicals safely.
- [Avoid burns](https://bitcoinuniverseio.github.io/atomicals-and-arc-20/guides/avoid-burns/) [protocol-behavior]: The working procedure that prevents every burn shape, with the executed cases that show what each one looks like.
- [Buy on the marketplace](https://bitcoinuniverseio.github.io/atomicals-and-arc-20/guides/buy-on-marketplace/) [universe-implementation]: Reserve, prepare, sign, and broadcast, with the checks that stop you paying for something that already moved.
- [Choose a wallet](https://bitcoinuniverseio.github.io/atomicals-and-arc-20/guides/choose-a-wallet/) [protocol-behavior]: The capabilities that make a wallet safe for Atomicals, how to test for them in ten minutes, and what to do if yours fails.
- [Claim a Realm](https://bitcoinuniverseio.github.io/atomicals-and-arc-20/guides/claim-a-realm/) [protocol-behavior]: Request a top-level name, confirm it resolved to you, and protect the output that carries it.
- [Claim a Subrealm](https://bitcoinuniverseio.github.io/atomicals-and-arc-20/guides/claim-a-subrealm/) [protocol-behavior]: Satisfy a parent Realm's rules, including any payment, and confirm you actually won the name.
- [Confirmations and reorgs](https://bitcoinuniverseio.github.io/atomicals-and-arc-20/guides/confirmations-and-reorgs/) [protocol-behavior]: When an Atomicals result is settled enough to act on, and what changes when the chain reorganises.
- [Create a Container](https://bitcoinuniverseio.github.io/atomicals-and-arc-20/guides/create-a-container/) [protocol-behavior]: Mint a collection identity, confirm the name resolved, and prepare for item minting without locking in a mistake.
- [Create DMINT items](https://bitcoinuniverseio.github.io/atomicals-and-arc-20/guides/create-dmint-items/) [protocol-behavior]: Seal the manifest before opening minting, and check what is on chain before making it permanent.
- [Deploy a fixed DFT](https://bitcoinuniverseio.github.io/atomicals-and-arc-20/guides/deploy-fixed-dft/) [protocol-behavior]: Publish the mint rules others will claim against, and get the four parameters right the first time.
- [Deploy a perpetual DFT](https://bitcoinuniverseio.github.io/atomicals-and-arc-20/guides/deploy-perpetual-dft/) [protocol-behavior]: An activation gated mode with progressing Bitwork, and the display rule that stops you publishing a supply cap that does not exist.
- [Direct FT issuance](https://bitcoinuniverseio.github.io/atomicals-and-arc-20/guides/direct-ft-issuance/) [protocol-behavior]: One transaction, one complete supply, and the bitcoin you must actually commit for it.
- [Fees and costs](https://bitcoinuniverseio.github.io/atomicals-and-arc-20/guides/fees-and-costs/) [protocol-behavior]: Everything you actually pay for an Atomicals action, including the costs people forget until they have already spent them.
- [Inspect an ARC-20 ticker](https://bitcoinuniverseio.github.io/atomicals-and-arc-20/guides/inspect-a-ticker/) [universe-implementation]: Resolve a name to the Atomical that actually holds it, and read the deployment before you trust any figure about it.
- [Inspect an address](https://bitcoinuniverseio.github.io/atomicals-and-arc-20/guides/inspect-an-address/) [universe-implementation]: Read outpoints instead of totals, and understand exactly what a balance figure hides.
- [Inspect an Atomical](https://bitcoinuniverseio.github.io/atomicals-and-arc-20/guides/inspect-an-atomical/) [universe-implementation]: Read identity, location, history, and sealed state, and know which of the four you are actually looking at.
- [List an ARC-20 lot](https://bitcoinuniverseio.github.io/atomicals-and-arc-20/guides/list-an-arc20-lot/) [universe-implementation]: Prove ownership, prepare a listing, sign it, and finalise, without exposing the asset to an unbound signature.
- [List an NFT, Realm, or Subrealm](https://bitcoinuniverseio.github.io/atomicals-and-arc-20/guides/list-an-nft-or-realm/) [universe-implementation]: The same lifecycle as an ARC-20 lot, plus the extra name check the Realm lanes carry.
- [Mint an Atomicals NFT](https://bitcoinuniverseio.github.io/atomicals-and-arc-20/guides/mint-an-nft/) [protocol-behavior]: Build the payload, choose an output value, and understand which decisions become permanent.
- [Mint ARC-20](https://bitcoinuniverseio.github.io/atomicals-and-arc-20/guides/mint-arc20/) [protocol-behavior]: Claim against a deployment without wasting a fee on a claim that was never going to be valid.
- [Offers](https://bitcoinuniverseio.github.io/atomicals-and-arc-20/guides/offers/) [universe-implementation]: Make an offer, cancel it, and accept one, with the checks each side owes the other.
- [Prepare BTC and protected UTXOs](https://bitcoinuniverseio.github.io/atomicals-and-arc-20/guides/prepare-utxos/) [protocol-behavior]: Build a cardinal pool for fees so a coloured output is never selected by accident, and size your lots for the transfers you expect.
- [Protect coloured outputs](https://bitcoinuniverseio.github.io/atomicals-and-arc-20/guides/protect-colored-outputs/) [protocol-behavior]: The working separation between asset money and fee money, and the three habits that prevent an accidental spend.
- [Recover from a rejection](https://bitcoinuniverseio.github.io/atomicals-and-arc-20/guides/recover-from-a-rejection/) [protocol-behavior]: A transaction that has not confirmed is still recoverable. Here is how to work out which situation you are in.
- [Resolve Unicode names](https://bitcoinuniverseio.github.io/atomicals-and-arc-20/guides/resolve-unicode-names/) [protocol-behavior]: Normalise, compare, and detect confusable names before you act on one.
- [Split and combine ARC-20](https://bitcoinuniverseio.github.io/atomicals-and-arc-20/guides/split-and-combine-arc20/) [protocol-behavior]: Reshape your lots deliberately, and know when combining makes future transfers harder.
- [Transfer ARC-20](https://bitcoinuniverseio.github.io/atomicals-and-arc-20/guides/transfer-arc20/) [protocol-behavior]: Build a transfer that places every unit where you intend and burns nothing.
- [Unavailable index or empty balance](https://bitcoinuniverseio.github.io/atomicals-and-arc-20/guides/unavailable-indexer-vs-empty-balance/) [universe-implementation]: The difference between a service that cannot answer and an answer of zero, and why confusing them causes most false alarms.
- [Update or remove a listing](https://bitcoinuniverseio.github.io/atomicals-and-arc-20/guides/update-or-remove-a-listing/) [universe-implementation]: Change a price or delist, with the same ownership proof and the same failure-closed checks.
- [Verify a transaction](https://bitcoinuniverseio.github.io/atomicals-and-arc-20/guides/verify-a-transaction/) [protocol-behavior]: Confirm what a transaction actually did, before signing and after broadcast, including any burn it caused.
- [Verify settlement](https://bitcoinuniverseio.github.io/atomicals-and-arc-20/guides/verify-settlement/) [universe-implementation]: Confirm a trade actually completed, on chain and in the index, rather than trusting a status label.
- [Wallet signing failures](https://bitcoinuniverseio.github.io/atomicals-and-arc-20/guides/wallet-signing-failures/) [universe-implementation]: Diagnose a wallet that will not sign, by capability, encoding, and signature hash flag.

### develop

- [Architecture overview](https://bitcoinuniverseio.github.io/atomicals-and-arc-20/develop/) [universe-implementation]: How the Universe Atomicals services fit together, what each one is authoritative for, and where the boundaries are.
- [Authentication](https://bitcoinuniverseio.github.io/atomicals-and-arc-20/develop/authentication/) [universe-implementation]: What each Universe Atomicals surface requires, which credentials are public and which are internal, and what never appears in a browser.
- [Consistency and reorgs](https://bitcoinuniverseio.github.io/atomicals-and-arc-20/develop/consistency-and-reorgs/) [universe-implementation]: Generations, checkpoints, invalidation, and rollback, and what a consumer must do about each.
- [Data flow](https://bitcoinuniverseio.github.io/atomicals-and-arc-20/develop/data-flow/) [universe-implementation]: Where every number comes from, which hop can be stale, and what a consumer should record with each answer.
- [Errors](https://bitcoinuniverseio.github.io/atomicals-and-arc-20/develop/errors/) [universe-implementation]: The error envelope, the codes that matter, and how to tell a client mistake from a service state.
- [Idempotency and request IDs](https://bitcoinuniverseio.github.io/atomicals-and-arc-20/develop/idempotency-and-request-ids/) [universe-implementation]: Making a mutation safe to retry, and making a failure traceable afterwards.
- [Identifiers and networks](https://bitcoinuniverseio.github.io/atomicals-and-arc-20/develop/identifiers-and-networks/) [universe-implementation]: Protocol identifiers, network identifiers, asset identifiers, and the route prefix contract.
- [Migration](https://bitcoinuniverseio.github.io/atomicals-and-arc-20/develop/migration/) [universe-implementation]: Moving an integration between versions without discovering the differences in production.
- [Pagination and cursors](https://bitcoinuniverseio.github.io/atomicals-and-arc-20/develop/pagination-and-cursors/) [universe-implementation]: Signed cursors, what they bind to, and why a cursor stops working after a generation change.
- [Rate limits](https://bitcoinuniverseio.github.io/atomicals-and-arc-20/develop/rate-limits/) [universe-implementation]: Where a limit is actually implemented, where none exists, and how to behave well regardless.
- [Readiness and freshness](https://bitcoinuniverseio.github.io/atomicals-and-arc-20/develop/readiness-and-freshness/) [universe-implementation]: Configured, live, ready, degraded, stale, and mixed tip are six different states. A caller must handle each one differently.
- [Source of truth](https://bitcoinuniverseio.github.io/atomicals-and-arc-20/develop/source-of-truth/) [protocol-behavior]: The authority order every technical statement follows, and how to resolve two sources that disagree.
- [Versioning and deprecation](https://bitcoinuniverseio.github.io/atomicals-and-arc-20/develop/versioning-and-deprecation/) [universe-implementation]: What is versioned, how a breaking change is announced, and what a deprecation actually promises.

### reference

- [AI and agent access](https://bitcoinuniverseio.github.io/atomicals-and-arc-20/reference/ai-access/) [editorial]: Every machine readable output this documentation publishes, and what each one is for.
- [Universe ARC-20 API](https://bitcoinuniverseio.github.io/atomicals-and-arc-20/reference/api/arc20/) [universe-implementation]: The complete ARC-20 read contract, with its guarantees, its declared coverage limit, and the OpenAPI document behind it.
- [Universe NFT and Realm API](https://bitcoinuniverseio.github.io/atomicals-and-arc-20/reference/api/atomicals-nfts-realms/) [universe-implementation]: The complete read contract for plain NFTs, Realms, and Subrealms, including what the projection deliberately excludes.
- [Marketplace v1](https://bitcoinuniverseio.github.io/atomicals-and-arc-20/reference/api/marketplace-v1/) [universe-implementation]: The complete lifecycle, the signing contract, the exact PSBT shape, and everything the authority refuses.
- [Ordex contract](https://bitcoinuniverseio.github.io/atomicals-and-arc-20/reference/api/ordex/) [universe-implementation]: Where the Ordex marketplace contract, SDK, conformance vectors, and verifier live, and how the Universe boundary sits around them.
- [Atomicals CLI reference](https://bitcoinuniverseio.github.io/atomicals-and-arc-20/reference/cli/) [protocol-behavior]: Every command in the reference CLI, generated from the pinned source so the inventory cannot drift.
- [TypeScript client](https://bitcoinuniverseio.github.io/atomicals-and-arc-20/reference/client-sdk/) [universe-implementation]: A generated, strictly typed client for the public read APIs, with typed errors, pagination helpers, and no embedded secrets.
- [Conformance vectors](https://bitcoinuniverseio.github.io/atomicals-and-arc-20/reference/conformance/) [protocol-behavior]: The deterministic cases that back the prose, the interactive tools, and the tests, all executed from one engine.
- [ElectrumX reference](https://bitcoinuniverseio.github.io/atomicals-and-arc-20/reference/electrumx/) [protocol-behavior]: The Atomicals ElectrumX interface, what a Universe proxy adds, and where the boundary between them sits.
- [Documentation MCP server](https://bitcoinuniverseio.github.io/atomicals-and-arc-20/reference/mcp/) [universe-implementation]: A local, read-only server that lets an agent query this documentation without scraping HTML.
- [OpenAPI and downloads](https://bitcoinuniverseio.github.io/atomicals-and-arc-20/reference/openapi/) [universe-implementation]: Validated OpenAPI 3.1 documents, JSON Schemas, and every machine readable artefact this site publishes.
- [JSON Schemas](https://bitcoinuniverseio.github.io/atomicals-and-arc-20/reference/schemas/) [universe-implementation]: The shared component library, what each definition is for, and the rules it encodes.
- [Wallet integration](https://bitcoinuniverseio.github.io/atomicals-and-arc-20/reference/wallet-integration/) [universe-implementation]: Provider detection, capability discovery, PSBT encodings, signing scopes, and normalised errors.
- [SDKs](https://bitcoinuniverseio.github.io/atomicals-and-arc-20/sdks/) [universe-implementation]: Generated read-only clients for TypeScript, Python, Go, and Rust, all derived from the same OpenAPI contracts.
- [Workflows](https://bitcoinuniverseio.github.io/atomicals-and-arc-20/workflows/) [universe-implementation]: Machine-readable Arazzo workflows with generated curl, TypeScript, and JavaScript examples for every step.

### tools

- [Protocol Atlas](https://bitcoinuniverseio.github.io/atomicals-and-arc-20/protocol-atlas/) [editorial]: An evidence-backed, interactive comparison of Bitcoin token and digital-object protocols, with every fact pinned to a source revision.
- [Tools](https://bitcoinuniverseio.github.io/atomicals-and-arc-20/tools/) [editorial]: Local, read-only tools that model Atomicals behavior without ever signing, broadcasting, or sending your data anywhere.
- [ARC-20 allocation visualizer](https://bitcoinuniverseio.github.io/atomicals-and-arc-20/tools/allocation-visualizer/) [protocol-behavior]: Model a transaction and see exactly which output receives which units, and what burns, before you build anything.
- [API Conformance Workbench](https://bitcoinuniverseio.github.io/atomicals-and-arc-20/tools/api-conformance/) [universe-implementation]: Validate a live read-only endpoint against the published contracts, with a scrubbed report and no stored credentials.
- [API explorer](https://bitcoinuniverseio.github.io/atomicals-and-arc-20/tools/api-explorer/) [universe-implementation]: Browse every documented operation, parameter, and example, and copy a request to run in your own environment.
- [Bitwork estimator](https://bitcoinuniverseio.github.io/atomicals-and-arc-20/tools/bitwork-estimator/) [protocol-behavior]: Model a Bitwork prefix and see the expected search space, with the uncertainty stated rather than hidden.
- [CLI command builder](https://bitcoinuniverseio.github.io/atomicals-and-arc-20/tools/cli-builder/) [protocol-behavior]: Build a validated, copyable command from the pinned command inventory, with the safety implications shown.
- [Protocol comparison has moved](https://bitcoinuniverseio.github.io/atomicals-and-arc-20/tools/protocol-comparison/) [editorial]: The protocol comparison is now the Protocol Atlas, with evidence-backed cells, four synchronized views, and exports.
- [Protocol Lab](https://bitcoinuniverseio.github.io/atomicals-and-arc-20/tools/protocol-lab/) [protocol-behavior]: Construct and replay Atomicals workflows deterministically in the browser, with no keys, no signing, and no network.
- [Transaction safety inspector](https://bitcoinuniverseio.github.io/atomicals-and-arc-20/tools/transaction-inspector/) [protocol-behavior]: Parse a transaction or PSBT in your browser and read its inputs, outputs, and signature scope before you sign.
- [UTXO Safety Planner](https://bitcoinuniverseio.github.io/atomicals-and-arc-20/tools/utxo-safety/) [protocol-behavior]: Classify asset-bearing UTXOs, see the risks, and generate deterministic candidate plans before you construct a transaction.
